title: The One Question Your Broker Cannot Answer in Presale Sales

keywords: what will I see from my window presale
body:
There is one question presale brokers hear every day, and most of them cannot answer it. It is not about price, interest rates or the market. It is much simpler than that: what do I see from my window?

## The moment the deal starts to slow down

Picture the scene. A buyer is interested in a unit on the 7th floor, facing north. They ask what the view will be. The broker opens the marketing materials, and the only view on hand is the penthouse rendering. So the broker says what brokers often say: well, something like this.

The buyer smiles. The buyer goes home. And then the buyer starts to think.

Nothing went wrong in the meeting. There was no objection, no argument. But a doubt walked out of the room with the buyer, and that doubt is now doing the talking.

## Why the penthouse view is the wrong answer

A view from the top of the tower says nothing about a unit on the 7th floor. The height is different. The direction may be different. What sits across the street looks very different from low down. The buyer knows this, even if nobody says it out loud.

So something like this is not an answer. It is a polite way of saying we do not know. And when you are asking someone to buy a home that does not exist yet, not knowing is exactly what they are afraid of.

## Not the price, not the market, a simple doubt

In my experience, this single question is where many presale deals slow down or quietly die. Developers look for the problem in the price or in the market. Often the real problem is smaller and easier to fix: a buyer who could not picture their own unit.

## Give your broker the answer for every unit

The fix is to make sure your brokers can answer for every unit, not just the best one:

1. **The real view** from each unit, not a generic rendering.
2. **From the real floor**, at the right height.
3. **In the right direction**, north, south, east or west, the way the windows actually face.

When the broker can show the buyer exactly what they will see, the conversation changes. The doubt has nothing to grow on, and the question disappears.

So here is a simple test for your sales team: if a buyer asked about the 7th floor, north side, today, what would they be shown?
takeaways: Presale buyers constantly ask what they will see from their own window.
Showing the penthouse rendering and saying something like this does not answer the question.
The buyer leaves with a doubt, and that doubt is where deals slow down or die.
Often the problem is not price or the market, but a buyer who cannot picture their unit.
Give brokers the real view from the real floor for every unit, and the question disappears.
faq: What do presale buyers ask most often?
One of the most common questions is what they will see from their window, meaning the real view from their specific floor and direction.
Why do presale deals slow down?
In my experience, many slow down because of a simple doubt, such as a buyer who cannot picture the view from their own unit, rather than because of price or the market.
Can a penthouse rendering show the view from a lower floor?
No. The view changes with height and direction, so a penthouse rendering does not tell a buyer what they will see from a unit lower down.
